Subject: EU-only processing for HealthCore — SCCs + deletion proof

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. HealthCore's Privacy and Legal teams have reviewed Redwood's in-region capabilities and we need to formalize requirements before we proceed. High level: HealthCore requires EU-only processing for all customer-provided PII for the pilot, and wants contractual SCCs plus operational evidence of deletion for test and production data when requested.

Could you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can commit to processing, backups, and logs staying within EU regions for the pilot (no cross-border copies).
- If SCCs are in scope when Redwood acts as subprocessors and whether you have a standardized SCCs Annex we can review.
- The type of evidence you can provide for deletion requests (audit logs, KMS key destruction events, snapshot deletion timelines). We will likely need timestamped proofs and an attestation.

We're trying to map this into a mutual action plan with expected artifacts and timelines. Can you loop in legal/security?

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Data Protection Officer
HealthCore

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthcore.org>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 03 Sep 2028 08:22:00 +0100
Subject: Technical evidence / in-region guarantees (details)

Elena and Jordan — following up with the technical detail you'll need to scope the MAP. I kept this high-level and can expand any area you flag.

EU-only processing: we offer an EU-exclusive cluster option (hosted in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). When you select "EU-only" in the deployment config we do not route or replicate inference requests outside those regions.

Backups & snapshots:
- Primary snapshots and scheduled backups for EU-only customers are stored in region; cross-region backups are not enabled unless customer requests.
- We retain backups for a customer-configurable retention window (default 30 days for trial, configurable 0–90 days for enterprise).

KMS / keys:
- Data encryption at rest via customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key on EU KMS key possible for Private deployments).
- We record KMS key rotation and key-deletion events in a tamper-evident log (hash-chained).

Deletion proof types we can provide:
1) Snapshot deletion events with timestamps and S3-like object deletion receipts.
2) Audit log excerpts showing deletion operation IDs, actor, and request IDs.
3) KMS key rotation/disable events (if BYOK used) that show loss of ability to decrypt old ciphertext.
4) Runbook-based attestation: an engineer-signed PDF showing steps taken and confirmation of artifact removal.

What we need from HealthCore to scope evidence deliverable:
- Exact retention policy you want applied to the pilot (e.g., session-level data retained 7 days, transcript retention 30 days, embeddings retained 90 days, etc.).
- Acceptance criteria for "proof of deletion" (do you need raw object IDs, hashes, or is a signed attestation + log excerpts sufficient?).

Attachments: I attached our redwood-sccs-evidence-checklist.pdf that maps artifacts we can provide to common ask types.

If HealthCore requires legally certified erasure (not just technical deletion), we'll flag that to legal for contract language.

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call — propose Tue 05 Sep 09:00 CET.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sccs-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks Naomi — helpful summary. A few clarifications from Legal:

1) SCCs: please share the standardized SCCs Annex and confirm which clause(s) cover subprocessors. We need to confirm you accept liability limits in our DPA template or note any carve-outs.

2) Proof of deletion: HealthCore's policy requires (a) an immutable log of deletion operations, (b) object IDs or hashes to correlate to our records, and (c) signed attestation within 5 business days for production deletion requests. Is that feasible for Redwood?

3) Backups: we cannot accept a scenario where backup retention implicitly allows recovery beyond the customer-specified window. If restoration requires a separate legal/operational request, please state that clearly.

If you can provide a short MAP (deliverables + owner + target dates) we'll circulate it internally.

Regards,
Daniel Reilly
Counsel, HealthCore

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: EU-only processing for HealthCore — SCCs + deletion proof

Daniel — thanks. Short answers:
- SCCs Annex: Lauren will attach the standard addendum and call out subprocessors clause (we accept SCCs as controller->processor flows; as a processor/subprocessor we sign the annex and maintain subprocessor list).
- Proof of deletion timeline: We can commit to providing signed attestation + immutable log excerpts within 5 business days for production deletions. For emergency/urgent requests we have an escalation path for 48–72 hour turnaround depending on scope.
- Backups: Recovery from backups requires an authenticated request and is governed by the MAP; by default we will not restore backups beyond the configured retention window without your explicit approval.

Attached is a 1-page MAP draft and a link to a read-only Drive folder with sample artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcd_HealthCore-SCCS-Evidence (read-only). I'll create JIRA PRV-8241 to track the engineering tasks.

Action items (we own):
A. Lauren: SCCs addendum + proposed DPA redlines (2 business days).
B. Naomi: finalize evidence checklist and confirm what object-level IDs/log formats we can export (3 business days).
C. Jordan: deliver MAP and schedule follow-up call (this thread).

Please confirm HealthCore's desired retention settings for pilot so Naomi can scope exports accurately.

Best,
Jordan

Subject: Final technical scope for MAP — evidence & erasure runbook

Elena / Daniel — following our notes and the MAP draft, below is the technical scope we will deliver for the pilot. If this matches HealthCore's requirements, we'll lock it into the MAP and target delivery dates (see end).

Scope (evidence types):
- Full deletion package for each erasure request including:
  * Deletion request ID and timestamp (our internal request GUID).
  * Audit log excerpt (actor, operation, resource IDs, request IDs).
  * Object IDs / bucket/archive keys + CRC hashes we can provide to correlate.
  * Snapshot deletion receipts (storage-level deletion timestamps).
  * KMS event: key-rotation or key-disable record when BYOK is used.
  * Engineer-signed attestation PDF summarizing steps and confirming no remaining recoverable copies.

Operational constraints / notes:
- Retention controls: recommend the pilot use the following policy so evidence scope is manageable: session transcripts — 7 days; model inputs/outputs (non-sensitive) — 30 days; embeddings — 90 days. We can adjust based on your legal team's target.
- Backup windows: backups will be pruned according to retention; we will not retain restorations beyond the configured window without a formal request that will be logged and approved.
- Timeline: standard production deletion attestation will be delivered within 5 business days; emergency scope we can accelerate to 48–72 hours but may require an SOW for frequent expedited requests.

Next actions & target dates:
- Lauren to share SCCs Annex and DPA redlines by Thu 07 Sep EOD (Lauren).
- Naomi to generate a sample deletion package for a test erasure request and upload to the Drive folder by Fri 08 Sep EOD (Naomi).
- Jordan to schedule MAP review call for Mon 11 Sep 09:00 CET.

I'll attach an internal playbook draft (proof-of-deletion-playbook.pdf) to this thread when the sample is uploaded. If you agree, we'll proceed to lock the MAP and circulate a DocuSign-ready DPA + SCCs Annex for signature.

—Naomi
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
